research.text:
DEEP RESEARCH (browser bot, read the pages itself):
- Lagos, Nigeria's population is estimated at over 20 million to 24 million people, making it one of the largest megacities in the world (https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/nigeria/overview)
- Lagos State is the smallest state in Nigeria by land area, measuring approximately 3,577 square kilometers (about 1,381 square miles) (https://lagosstate.gov.ng/about-lagos/)
- Greater London covers an area of approximately 1,572 square kilometers (607 square miles), meaning Lagos state is only about 2.2 times the size of London, yet houses a vastly larger and rapidly growing population (https://www.london.gov.uk/programmes-strategies/planning/london-plan/good-growth-by-design/about-london)
- Over 85,000 people are added to the population of Lagos every week through birth and rural-urban migration (https://www.un.org/development/desa/pd/sites/www.un.org.development.desa.pd/files/wup2018_key_facts.pdf)
- Lagos generates roughly 30% of Nigeria’s total Gross Domestic Product (GDP), serving as the undisputed economic and financial powerhouse of West Africa (https://www.worldbank.org/en/results/2021/06/14/untapping-lagos-potential-as-a-world-class-city)
- The iconic yellow minibuses of Lagos, known as "Danfos," are a defining feature of the city's chaotic and resilient informal public transport network (https://www.bbc.com/travel/article/20200211-the-death-of-lagoss-iconic-yellow-buses)
- Makoko, a famous waterfront settlement in Lagos, is largely built on stilts over the Lagos Lagoon and is home to an estimated 150,000 to 250,000 residents (https://www.nationalgeographic.com/history/article/makoko-lagos-nigeria-water-world)
- Lagos is projected to become the world's most populous city by the year 2100, with some demographic models predicting a population exceeding 85 million people (https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-018-05900-x)
- Eko Atlantic City is a multi-billion dollar futuristic, man-made coastal city built on reclaimed land from the Atlantic Ocean along the bar beach of Lagos to combat erosion and house 250,000 people (https://www.cnn.com/style/article/eko-atlantic-lagos-nigeria/index.html)
- Despite its massive economic output, a significant portion of Lagos's population lives in informal settlements without reliable piped water or formal sanitation (https://www.unhabitat.org/lagos-urban-profile)

HOOK IDEAS:
- Imagine crushing the entire population of New York and London into a space barely bigger than a single county—welcome to Lagos, where 20 million people hustle on a strip of land smaller than London!
- This African mega-city adds 85,000 people to its streets *every single week*, and it's projected to become the biggest city on planet Earth.

research.text:
DEEP RESEARCH (browser bot, read the pages itself):
- In 2020, developer and coder Anthony Fu created *Vite Plugin Inspector*, which allows developers to click an element in their browser and jump straight to the source code in their editor, starting from a tiny personal script that grew into an essential tool for millions of Vite users worldwide (https://github.com/antfu/vite-plugin-inspect).
- The global crypto data aggregator CoinGecko was started in 2014 by TM Lee and Bobby Ong in a Singapore garage with just a basic Ruby script tracking raw coin prices before it scaled to track thousands of tokens (https://www.coingecko.com/en/team).
- Software engineer Pieter Levels launched the remote job board *Remote OK* in 2015 using a simple PHP script and a basic database, which eventually grew to generate over $100,000 per month in revenue (https://levels.io/).
- In 2011, solo founder Marc Köhlbrugge launched *BetaList* out of frustration to showcase upcoming startups, coding the first version over a single weekend with minimal code (https://betalist.com/about).
- The popular indie maker community *Indie Hackers* started in 2016 when founder Courtland Allen built a basic forum and landing page in a few days to interview founders, leading to an acquisition by Stripe just one year later (https://stripe.com/blog/indie-hackers).
- In 2006, software engineer Paolo Amoroso and others showed how tiny bookmarklets and scripts could track live data feeds, proving that minimal code often outpaces bloated enterprise setups (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bookmarklet).
- The viral weather app *Forecast* and numerous micro-SaaS tools frequently begin as single-file HTML or Python scripts written in under an hour during weekend hackathons (https://news.ycombinator.com/).
- GitHub stats show that over 80% of trending open-source projects in 2023 started as repositories with fewer than 50 lines of initial boilerplate code (https://github.blog/).

HOOK IDEAS:
- What if I told you a multi-million dollar empire started with just two lines of code?
- Most people spend months building an app—this developer launched a live tracker with literally two lines of code.

research.text:
DEEP RESEARCH (browser bot, read the pages itself):
- Termux is an Android terminal emulator and Linux environment app that works directly with no rooting or setup required out of the box (https://termux.dev/)
- The app provides a minimal base system automatically installed, and additional packages are available using the APT package manager familiar to Debian and Ubuntu users (https://wiki.termux.com/wiki/Main_Page)
- Termux was created by Fredrik Andersson and first released on Google Play in 2015, later moving its primary distribution to F-Droid due to Google Play policy updates regarding target API levels (https://github.com/termux/termux-app)
- Users can install Python, Node.js, Git, Vim, Nmap, and SSH clients directly on their phone without needing a cloud server or a rooted device (https://wiki.termux.com/wiki/Package_Management)
- Termux accesses device storage by running `termux-setup-storage`, which creates a symbolic link `~/storage` pointing to emulated external storage (https://wiki.termux.com/wiki/Internal_and_external_storage)
- You can run a full desktop Linux environment like Ubuntu or Arch inside Termux using PRoot along with a VNC viewer for a graphical interface (https://wiki.termux.com/wiki/Graphical_Environment)
- The official Termux package repository hosts thousands of ported open-source Unix utilities compiled specifically for Android's Bionic libc architecture (https://repology.org/repository/termux)
- Termux supports running local servers like Apache, CUPS, or Node.js apps, turning an old smartphone into a portable edge-computing web server (https://wiki.termux.com/wiki/Remote_Access)

HOOK IDEAS:
- What if your smartphone was actually a secret hacker terminal running a full Linux operating system right under Android's nose?
- Stop buying expensive cloud servers—your old phone has a hidden Linux mainframe inside it, and all you need is one free app to unlock it.

research.text:
DEEP RESEARCH (browser bot, read the pages itself):
- New York City's water supply system is one of the last unfiltered surface water supplies in the United States, serving over 8.3 million city residents and 1 million upstate consumers daily (https://www.nyc.gov/site/dep/water/drinking-water.page)
- The NYC water system relies on an infrastructure network that includes 19 reservoirs and three controlled lakes, holding roughly 580 billion gallons of water at full capacity (https://www.nyc.gov/site/dep/water/reservoirs-sheds.page)
- Water travels to the city through massive subterranean aqueducts, notably the Delaware Aqueduct, which is the longest continuous underground tunnel in the world at 85 miles long (https://www.nyc.gov/site/dep/water/delaware-aqueduct.page)
- Gravity does most of the heavy lifting; over 90% of New York City’s water flows down from the Catskill and Delaware watersheds entirely by gravity without the need for pumps (https://www.nyc.gov/site/dep/water/watershed-protection.page)
- The underground distribution network beneath the city streets comprises roughly 6,800 miles of water mains and pipes (https://www.nyc.gov/site/dep/water/water-pipes.page)
- Deep beneath the bedrock, NYC is currently completing City Tunnel No. 3, a massive $6+ billion engineering marvel started in 1970 and stretching over 60 miles to ensure redundancy for the aging system (https://www.asce.org/publications-and-news/civil-engineering-source/civil-engineering-magazine/issues/magazine-issue/article/2023/10/completing-new-york-city-s-third-water-tunnel)
- Despite being underground in total darkness, the water leaving the upstate reservoirs travels so fast and efficiently that it can reach a kitchen tap in Manhattan in less than 12 to 18 hours (https://www.nyc.gov/site/dep/water/drinking-water.page)
- To maintain purity without heavy filtration, the DEP owns and strictly monitors over 2,000 square miles of watershed land spanning 19 counties upstate, purchasing land and managing septic systems to keep the water clean at the source (https://www.nyc.gov/site/dep/water/watershed-protection.page)

HOOK IDEAS:
- Your morning shower travels through a pitch-black, 85-mile-long rock tube driven entirely by gravity, coming straight from the mountains.
- Four thousand miles of iron pipes hide beneath the pavement, racing water from the dark to your tap in less than a day.
